newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks retreat from high to close slightly up.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks retreat from high to close slightly up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks retreated from an all-time high to close Wednesday just slightly higher following late profit-taking in blue chips, particularly Hong Kong Telecommunications, brokers said.
"There is little selling pressure, just profit-taking," said Priscilla Cheung, dealing director at Dao Heng Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed 16.32 points, or 0.11 percent, higher at 14,556.48 after setting a new intra-day high at 14,688.47 late in the morning session.
Turnover was a heavy HK$16.95 billion, slightly lower than Tuesday's hefty HK$17.92 billion.
The index moved in record territory for most of the day, boosted by buying in HSBC Holdings, speculative interest in Hongkong Telecom and some shortcovering in the futures market, brokers said.
"Futures were quite strong and there obviously was a short squeeze," said Franco Tong, in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong. "The market has gone a lot further than many people expected."
The June Hang Seng Index contract rose to a high of 14,790 in early afternoon, a healthy premium to even the cash market's record high.
But the rally reversed course in the afternoon. The May contract, which expires on Thursday, closed 15 points lower at 14,555, while the June contract ended 20 points lower at 14,605.
Defensive utility issues outperformed the market, followed closely by banks. Properties and the commercial and industrial sector lost ground.

Hongkong Telecom rose to a year high of HK$17.75 then eased to close at HK$0.20 higher at HK$17.00 on heavy turnover of HK$1.18 billion. Rumours of that various Chinese institutions were interested in acquiring a stake in the company have fuelled speculative interest in the stock, brokers said.
HSBC Holdings also set a record at HK$230.00 then eased to close HK$3.00 higher at HK$229.00 on heavy trade of HK$770.47 million.
Individuals trading in red chips remained a dominant theme of the market, brokers said.
Laggard red chips Guangdong Investment added HK$0.20 to HK$9.50 and China Overseas Land put on HK$0.175 to HK$4.90.
Mid caps also strongly outperformed the index. Dah Sing Financial Holdings added HK$0.90 to HK$37.90.
